Subject: POC kickoff — routing policy tabletop + load tests (week of Jun 20)

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. PillarHealth is ready to move into a short POC to validate routing policies and failover behavior for our clinical summarization flow. High-level asks: prompt review & prompt sets, model candidate validation (latency + quality), fallback tiers, and scaled load tests to simulate peak traffic.

Can we lock 2 half-days: one tabletop to walk policy decisions and prompts, and one load day for traffic and KV/prefix caching checks? Our engineering window is the week of Jun 20 — preferred times are mornings PT.

Attendees on our side: me (EM), Alex Ruiz (cloud ops).

Would you be able to propose times and a rough agenda? Also please include any prework we should complete.

Best,
Emma

Head of Integrations, PillarHealth

Hi Emma — thanks, this is perfect.

Proposal:
- Day 1 (Tabletop): Wed Jun 23, 9:00–12:00 PT — agenda: prompt review, model candidate matrix, fallback tiering, region mapping, acceptance criteria.
- Day 2 (Load day): Thu Jun 24, 8:30–12:30 PT — agenda: progressive traffic ramp, KV cache warmup, failure-injection scenarios, throughput/latency measurement.

Prework for PillarHealth: share representative prompt sets (5–10 per flow) and expected QPS during peak. We’ll prep a short model comparison (latency/quality) based on your prompts and propose 2 candidate stacks (one lower-cost quantized, one higher-quality non-quant).

I’m attaching a draft POC test plan and an initial routing agenda for review. Can you confirm attendees and whether you prefer combining the days into a single longer session?

Thanks — I’ve looped in Marissa (CS lead) and Rishi (tech owner) so they can run the load tests / model tuning.

Sooj

Subject: Internal: PillarHealth POC — who owns what for Jun 23/24

Team — quick internal coordination for the PillarHealth kickoff:

Plan: tabletop on Wed 6/23 9–12 PT, load day Thu 6/24 8:30–12:30 PT (Emma asked mornings).

Asks:
- Marissa: lead the session intro and acceptance criteria, own client liaison during tabletop.
- Rishi: run the load harness and bring the load scripts, coordinate prefix caching instrumentation and KV warmup timing.
- Laura: prepare the model candidate short-list and quantized runtimes (redwood-llama-13b-q4_0, rwd-13b-int8), plus a brief on fallback rules (cold-start fallbacks -> smaller model, region failover).

Also flagging two decisions we must be ready to make in the tabletop:
1) Whether to use multi-region active-active (us-west + eu-central) or single primary with cross-region fallback.
2) Tiering: what token latency threshold triggers immediate fallback vs queued degradation.

I attached the draft files. Please confirm you can run the load day and report back any infra conflicts by EOD Tue.

Thanks,
Soojin
